title: Quantum Magnonics: Quantum States Generation and Applications
authors: Zi-Xu Lu, Xuan Zuo, Xin-Lei Hei, Gang Liu, Zeng-Xing Liu, Qi Guo, Peng-Bo Li, Jie Li
abstract: Hybrid systems based on magnons in ferromagnetic materials, such as yttrium iron garnet, have achieved remarkable development in the last decade. These include the coupling of magnons to microwave and optical photons, superconducting qubits, phonons, spins, the center-of-mass motion of a ferromagnet, etc. Here, we review both the experimental and theoretical progress in this field, focusing on the generation of magnonic quantum states and their applications in a broad range of fields. Since the strong coupling is a prerequisite for achieving coherent quantum control of magnons and preparing magnonic quantum states, we start by introducing representative strong-coupling experiments in cavity magnonics, then review a series of protocols for creating various magnonic quantum states, such as Fock, cat, squeezed, and entangled states, and discuss their potential applications in macroscopic quantum studies, quantum information science, quantum sensing, magnonic quantum devices, dark matter detection, and so on. Finally, we summarize the review and give an outlook for the future study of quantum magnonics.
summary: This review comprehensively surveys the field of quantum magnonics, detailing how hybrid systems couple magnons in ferromagnets to other quantum elements like photons and qubits. It outlines protocols for generating advanced quantum states—such as entangled or cat states—and discusses their potential utility in quantum sensing and information processing.
main_problem: The review surveys the experimental and theoretical progress of quantum magnonics, focusing on generating complex quantum states and exploring diverse applications.
main_result: Strong coupling in hybrid systems allows for the preparation of various non-classical states (Fock, cat, squeezed, entangled) using magnons coupled to photons, qubits, and phonons.
method: The review synthesizes theoretical protocols alongside experimental demonstrations across multiple physical platforms.
model_or_system: The core system involves magnons in ferromagnetic materials (like YIG), modeled via bosonic operators derived from the Heisenberg model. These are coupled to external systems such as microwave/optical cavities, superconducting qubits, and mechanical oscillators.
key_observables: Magnon-photon entanglement, Bell states fidelity, quantum state purity (e.g., cat states), and nonreciprocal transmission.
important_parameters: Strong coupling regime ($g \gg \kappa, \gamma$), magnon dispersion relation ($\hbar\omega_k$), and coupling strengths ($g_{ma}, g_{mb}$).
main_assumptions: The analysis often relies on the strong coupling prerequisite for coherent control, sometimes utilizing approximations like the Rotating Wave Approximation (RWA).
figures_summary: Figures illustrate hybrid systems coupled to various excitations (M.W., Opt., acoustic, spins, qubits) and show experimental setups for cavity magnonics.
paper_structure: The review is structured by coupling type: microwave cavities, superconducting qubits, optical cavities, NV-center spins, and center-of-mass motion, detailing state generation protocols within each section.
why_interesting: This work bridges condensed matter magnetism with quantum optics and information science, providing concrete pathways to engineer quantum states using solid-state magnetic excitations.
